description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of modern control theory, covering digital control systems, nonlinear control fundamentals, optimal control principles, and adaptive control methodologies. The syllabus emphasizes modeling, stability analysis, controller design, and real-world applications across these four major domains of advanced control engineering.

syllabus.title: Digital Control Systems
syllabus.body: Digital control design concepts; sampling, quantization, reconstruction; discretization methods (impulse/step invariance, bilinear transform, finite-difference); discrete-time modeling using pulse transfer functions and state-space forms; time/frequency response of discrete systems; stability analysis using z-plane, Jury test, and Lyapunov methods; basics of digital controller design (PID, lead/lag compensators).

syllabus.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
syllabus.body: Characteristics and effects of nonlinearities; phase-plane analysis and phase portraits; singular points and qualitative behavior; describing function and quasi-linearization; limit cycles, bifurcation, jump resonance; Lyapunov-based methods for stability of nonlinear systems.

syllabus.title: Optimal Control
syllabus.body: Optimal control fundamentals and performance indices; calculus of variations and optimality conditions; Hamiltonian and Pontryagin's Minimum Principle; design of linear quadratic regulator (LQR); overview of Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control; basics of dynamic programming and Bellman's principle; engineering applications of optimal control.

syllabus.title: Adaptive Control
syllabus.body: Introduction to adaptive control; types of adaptive control (direct, indirect, hybrid); model reference adaptive control (MRAC); self-tuning regulators; parameter estimation and convergence in adaptive systems; applications in robotics, process control, and aerospace. Industry-oriented case studies: hands-on simulation modules for real-time advanced control implementation, visits to Siemens Centre of Excellence (SCoE) Labs, seminars, workshops, etc.

outcomes: Understand the principles, modeling, and stability analysis of digital control systems.
Analyze nonlinear system behavior and apply nonlinear control techniques for stability and control design.
Apply optimal control concepts including LQR/LQG and Pontryagin's principles for optimal controller design.
Design adaptive controllers and understand parameter estimation, MRAC, and self-tuning regulators.
